prompt:
How many separate EFFECTS does this person attempt? An effect is one of: wearing a thing down, restoring or sharpening it, revealing what is true of it by examining it, concealing something, exposing something hidden, making a noise, opening or closing a way out, going out through one, taking or handing over a thing, or moving a person. Moving her own body from one part of the room to another is NOT an effect: the room is one place and nothing records where in it she stands, so walking over to a thing, stepping back, turning, or standing somewhere is never counted. But CHANGING HER POSTURE is an effect on her own posture, like any other: going from on her feet to seated, kneeling, crouching or lying on the floor, or rising from one of those to her feet. Standing or leaning while already on her feet changes nothing and is not counted. TAKING a thing is a change of WHO HOLDS it. Picking something up to look at it and setting it down again is not a take, and is part of the act it prepares; taking it away from someone, or out of the room, is. A clause that says HOW an act is done is not a separate effect: "with my hand hidden by my body", "keeping the motion small", "while talking to her". A clause with its own ACTIVE VERB is: "use my body to shield the motion", "rock the tile with my knee". Examining counts as ONE effect (revealing), even though it changes nothing; looking for several details on one thing is still one. Speaking, watching and waiting are not effects. Answer with a single number and nothing else.
